Their Lemma 5.4 verifies C6 relative derivative Hölder control and uniform contractions. Summing log-derivative oscillations along contracting suffixes gives word-independent bounded distortion D. The s_U-conformal cylinder identity, quasi-multiplicativity p(uv)≈p(u)p(v) and boundedness of shift-pushforwards yield an invariant equivalent measure ν* with cylinders comparable by constants uniform in word length; this agrees with their Proposition C.4 uniqueness. Thus ν*{K0≥k}≈exp[−(2πs_U/|κ|)k] and the same conditional bound holds after any finite prefix. Iterating conditional avoidance gives the two finite-horizon powers and geometric bounds on mean first-hit time. Borel–Cantelli on dyadic horizons with thresholds (1±δ)log n/β establishes M_n/log n→1/β a.s., where β=2πs_U/|κ|. Source material explicitly checked for these nonstandard premises; no finite simulation was substituted. The law concerns invariant Cantor probability, not ambient Lebesgue initial data.
